items.title: CAS says IIHF didn’t provide sufficient evidence to prevent Russia from playing in international tournaments
items.summary: Multiple nations have already announced they would boycott playing against Russia in tournament competition, with multiple sponsors also threatening to pull out if action isn’t taken.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Photo from Anders Marshall/Euro The Court of Arbitration for Sport released a public statement on Thursday afternoon, saying the International Ice Hockey Federation “did not present sufficient evidence to establish the legal requirements for the non-participation of Russian teams.” The CAS recently ruled that the Russian Ice Hockey Federation would be allowed to enter teams in IIHF events, such as the upcoming World Junior Championship in Alberta. Russia has been banned from IIHF competition since the nation invaded Ukraine shortly after the 2022 Beijing Olympics, which saw Russian athletes play under the ‘Russian Olympic Committee’ banner. The country was banned along with Belarus, which supported Russia during the war. According to the organization, both the RIHF and the IIHF submitted their disputes with the CAS to help solve the issue, with the CAS publishing their decision on Oct. 30. “The CAS Panel noted that the organisational consequences of this ruling, as well as the potential introduction of a neutrality regime, which are now at the centre of public debate, were neither substantiated by sufficient evidence nor sought by the IIHF during the proceedings. CAS cannot impose measures that have not been requested by the Parties,” Thursday’s CAS statement read. Multiple nations have already announced they would boycott playing against Russia in tournament competition, with multiple sponsors also threatening to pull out if action isn’t taken. The IIHF itself previously said they were disappointed in the decision from the CAS. Earlier this week, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney said Russians will not be permitted to play in the World Juniors. items.title: Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki returning to lineup vs. Mammoth
items.body: Montreal captain Nick Suzuki will return to the lineup Thursday night against the Utah Mammoth as the Canadiens look to rebound from Tuesday's historic loss to the Winnipeg Jets. Suzuki was ruled out for two to four weeks after defenceman Michael Kesselring's shot struck his left hand in the third period of Montreal's 2-1 loss to the San Jose Sharks on Oct. 20. The 27-year-old centre missed his first six contests after playing in 546 consecutive regular-season games to begin his career. The Canadiens (9-3-3) managed well without their captain, winning five straight games before falling 5-4 in overtime to the Jets in an epic collapse. Winnipeg rallied from 4-0 down with 2:39 remaining in regulation, making for the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history. Jakub Dobes will get the start as Montreal looks to respond against the visiting Mammoth (10-6-0). Suzuki will rejoin wingers Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovsky on the Canadiens' first line. After producing 101 points in 2025-26 — and winning the Selke Trophy as the league's best defensive forward — the London, Ont., native has five goals and seven assists through 12 games this season. Ivan Demidov remains out with a lower-body injury despite reaching the end of his two-to-four-week recovery timeline. The 20-year-old winger, who led all rookies in points with 62 last season, hasn't played since the Canadiens' second game on Oct. 3.

items.title: Mandated neck protection, high-sticking pucks permitted for 2026-27 PWHL season
items.summary: Among changes for Year 4, players can play the puck above their shoulders this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sarah Boeke/PWHL Ahead of its fourth season of operation, the Professional Women’s Hockey League is making some changes to its rulebook. On Thursday, the league announced a few tweaks ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, including clarifications on body checking, mandated neck protection, new high-sticking rules, and some experimentation with overtime during the preseason. Neck guards have been a point of contention around the game ever since Adam Johnson’s tragic passing in 2023 . Since then, the IIHF , USA Hockey , American Hockey League and the NHL have mandated the use of neck guards for their athletes. Now, the PWHL is requiring all players and goaltenders to wear cut-resistant neck protection during games, including pregame warmups. An interesting rule being implemented this year is that players can now knock the puck out of the air with their stick above the shoulders. Unlike previous years, the play is blown dead after the puck is knocked down by a player and either that player or their teammate touches the puck. Now, play can continue, regardless of who bats the puck out of the air. Also, players can score when deflecting the puck high in the air, eliminating the judgment call from on- and off-ice officials about whether a player’s stick was above the crossbar. A similar rule was adopted by the WCHA prior to the 2025-26 season. One point in the rule is that players can cradle the puck above their shoulders (a la the Michigan goal). However, if a player tries to cradle the puck on a penalty shot or shootout, the play will be blown dead and the shot will be complete. Body checking has been a welcome addition to the women’s game. Silovs wasn’t great last year, posting below-average numbers in many statistical categories, with an .888 SV% and a 3.07 GAA in 39 games. This season, his traditional metrics are slightly better, with a 2.98 GAA and an .889 SV% in nine games, but his underlying numbers are much better. According to MoneyPuck , Silovs’ goals saved above expected last year were -11.9, while this year he is +2.5. That improvement is also quite obvious when you watch him play, as the Penguins give up a ton of high-danger chances, and Silovs has kept them in quite a few games this season. Entering this year, Sergei Murashov was expected to become the starter at some point, but given the start he’s had this season, Silovs is going to have some say in how that plays out and could be the starter as the season wears on. The Penguins acquired Silovs from the Vancouver Canucks for a song (a 2027 fourth-round pick and Chase Stillman) during the summer of 2025. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources No player better represents the potential – and ultimate disappointment – of the Vancouver Canucks ‘ previous core of players better than Elias Pettersson. Sure, Quinn Hughes was the face of it, and his jumping ship to the Minnesota Wild triggered the Canucks’ current rebuild. But at the same time, the only wasted potential Hughes had in Vancouver was minimal playoff success. He rose to superstardom as one of the league’s top defensemen with the Canucks, won a Norris Trophy in 2024 and was still at the top of his game when he was traded, ensuring Vancouver received solid assets in return for him. He followed that up with another 66-point season in 2019-20 (this time in 68 games), but impressed come playoff time with seven goals and 18 points in 17 games as the Canucks came two goals (not counting two empty net goals) shy of a Western Conference Final appearance. items.title: Winnipeg Jets recall forward Brayden Yager from AHL
items.body: Forward Brayden Yager has been recalled from the AHL, the team announced on Thursday. Yager, 22, has made one NHL appearance this season, logging 14 minutes, one shot and one face-off win in an overtime loss to the Dallas Stars on Oct. 22. The 14th-overall pick in 2023 has played a total of four NHL games, the first three coming last season, but has yet to register a point with the Jets. He was drafted by the Pittsburgh Penguins and was later traded to Winnipeg in 2024. Yager has spent most of the 2026-27 campaign with the Manitoba Moose, racking up seven goals and five assists in 10 games. The Saskatchewan native played 68 games for the AHL club last season and posted 10 goals and 20 assists. He'll look to help the Jets build momentum as they enter Thursday on the heels of a historic comeback OT win over the Montreal Canadiens that snapped a nine-game winless skid.

items.title: Sharks’ Sherwood calls Kings ‘disrespectful,’ demands his teammates ‘do something about it’
items.summary: Adrian Kempe had a hat trick and Quinton Byfield scored twice as the Kings defeated the Sharks Wednesday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Griffin Hooper San Jose Sharks’ forward Kiefer Sherwood said his team was “disrespected” by the Los Angeles Kings during the Sharks’ 7-2 loss Wednesday night. Sherwood, who finished the night with two shots and 17:39 of ice time, “They were up 6-2, put their top power play out, (Kings’ forward Artemi) Panarin is blocking shots, celebrating to his bench. It’s disrespectful. Until we do something about it, things aren’t going to change unless we man up and do something about it.” Sherwood, now with two goals and eight points in 17 games this season, also said him and his teammates had just held a players-only meeting after the game. “We’re going to move forward here and we got a lot to learn,” he said. “Listen, it’s better to go through the growing pains now than later on, right? We’re going to stick together and get through it together, and we’re going to fix our mindset and our work ethic for the next game, and we’re going to get gritty.” “This one obviously sucks, but no one’s feeling sorry for themselves,” Sherwood added. “Until we do something about it, stuff’s not going to change.” The Sharks are now 7-9-1 with 15 points and losses in five of their last six games and seven of their last 10. Captain Macklin Celebrini, now in his third NHL season, leads the team in all offensive categories with six goals and 11 assists for 17 points . Four players are tied for second in points with 10: Will Smith, Michael Misa, Ivar Stenberg and Jacob Trouba. He immediately jumped to the NHL, scoring 14 goals and 26 points in 66 games, good for a ninth-place finish in Calder Trophy voting. Kane spent one more season with the Thrashers and remained with the team when they relocated, becoming the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets. His first season in Winnipeg is arguably his career-best campaign. The Vancouver, BC, native finished second on the team in scoring behind Blake Wheeler , registering 30 goals and 57 points in 74 games with a +11 rating. items.title: Prospects Report: Why top 2028 NHL Draft prospect Liam Pue is ‘an electric player’
items.summary: At age 16, Regina Pats star Liam Pue already is one of the most dangerous players in the WHL. There’s every reason to believe he’ll be a high pick in the 2028 NHL Draft, writes Mike Koreen.
items.body: Liam Pue first put on skates and hit the ice at age two at home in Langley, B.C., in the arms of his father, Jason. Liam was a quick learner, so much so that his mom, Kristin, joked to her husband, "Geez, he almost skates better than he walks." Because of that early ability, and with Liam wanting to follow his brother Landon —three years older — into hockey, his parents looked for programs to help their youngest son improve his skills. There was one problem, though. "We went through a season where he's skating pretty well for his age, but there's no programs," Jason recalled this week. "I started signing him up for programs, but I lied about his age." "I remember one day my wife had taken him to a skate and there was kind of a new coach on the ice working with Liam," Jason said. "After the skate, this coach came up to the parent-viewing area, and he opened the door, and he said, 'Whose kid is wearing the Datsyuk jersey?' My wife just buried her head cause she was like, 'Oh my goodness, he knows we lied about his age.' Finally, she kind of waved, and he just came up, and he said, 'Your kid is awesome.'" That first meeting with coach Curtis Fraser, a former pro player and cousin of ex-NHLer Colin Fraser, turned out to be the start of a long, productive partnership. For years, Liam Pue played under Fraser up an age group or two with a familiar group of teammates. Pue continued working with Fraser at the Langley Hockey Academy as a teenager. That development path, with much of it outside the Hockey Canada umbrella, turned out to be a perfect fit for Pue. The 16-year-old winger is in the midst of a fantastic first full season in the WHL with the Regina Pats and is considered a top candidate for the 2028 NHL Draft, alongside fellow fast riser and Pats teammate Maddox Schultz.

Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Seattle’s Berkly Catton preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to his goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 5:13 (14:47 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Vilmanis has first two-goal game, Panthers top Blackhawks to cap homestand
items.summary: Sandis Vilmanis had the first two-goal game of his career, Sam Reinhart provided a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-3 on Wednesday night to wrap up a three-game homestand.
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Sandis Vilmanis had the first two-goal game of his career, Sam Reinhart provided a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-3 on Wednesday night to wrap up a three-game homestand. Seth Jones scored against his former team and Carter Verhaeghe had a goal and an assist for the Panthers, who are 4-1-0 in their last five games and 7-3-0 in their past 10. Vilmanis added two assists to finish with four points. Florida improved to 9-0-1 when allowing three goals or fewer this season. Reinhart's goal was an empty-netter to seal the win with 1:27 left. Frank Nazar had two third-period goals and Roman Kantserov also scored for Chicago. Ethan Del Mastro got two assists — his first points of the season, and the first multi-point game of his career. Connor Bedard had two assists. The Blackhawks are 1-6-1 in their last eight games. They gave up the final five goals in a 5-2 home loss to Colorado on Monday, then got down 3-0 in Florida before Kantserov got Chicago on the board. By then, the Panthers were already in full control. Vilmanis scored 4:43 into the game, and Verhaeghe’s power-play goal was assisted by Brady Tkachuk and Matthew Tkachuk at 12:29 of the first. Jones beat former Florida goalie Spencer Knight — they were traded for one another in the deal that sent Jones to the Panthers — for a 3-0 lead in the second. Nazar beat Panthers goalie Jacob Markström on a short-handed breakaway to cut Florida’s lead midway through the third. Vilmanis struck again with 8:59 left, restoring the two-goal edge. Nazar got his second of the game with 3:51 left, but Reinhart scored his ninth of the season to all but end the Blackhawks' comeback hopes.

Fabian Zetterlund and Tim Stutzle assisted on the go-ahead goal as Ottawa and Amadio capitalized on a 3-on-2 break. Shane Pinto also scored for the Senators, tying the game at 1 at 11:33 of the second period. Peyton Krebs scored at the 14-minute mark of the first to give the Sabres the lead. Tage Thompson and Zach Benson assisted on Krebs' first goal of the season. Samuel Ersson made 24 saves in the win for the Senators, who entered the game having lost three of their last four games, including a 6-3 setback against Anaheim on Sunday. items.title: Canadiens’ Ivan Demidov fractured ankle in preseason
items.summary: Demidov has been out since early October with a lower-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Fans of the Montreal Canadiens have finally received some clarity regarding an injury to one of their top players. On Wednesday’s episode of DFO Insider with Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta, Dan Milstein, the agent of Canadiens winger Ivan Demidov, revealed that Demidov suffered a fractured ankle during the preseason. Demidov, 20, has been out since early October with what was classified as a lower-body injury. Despite sustaining the injury in the preseason, the Russian national was active to start the regular season, putting up a goal and an assist in two games before initially getting ruled out for two to four weeks. Now in early November, we’re at the tail end of that time frame, but Milstein suggested that Demidov is still weeks away from returning. “Ivan Demidov is getting ready. Probably a few more weeks or so, we’ll see him back in the lineup,” Milstein said. “Unfortunately, he had a fractured ankle in the preseason. It was bothering him but he continued playing for the two games. I saw him after the first game of the season in Toronto, he walked up to me and said ‘Hey, something is bothering (me), something is not right.’ Then he goes out, plays the second game and we did an MRI. Hopefully Ivan will be back on the ice in a very short while and he’ll help the Montreal Canadiens start winning some games.” Demidov is coming off a sterling rookie season, in which he notched 19 goals and 43 assists for 62 points in all 82 regular season games, finishing second in voting for the Calder Trophy. He then contributed three goals and six assists for nine points in Montreal’s 19 playoff games. The Canadiens will host the Utah Mammoth on Thursday to finish up a three-game home stand .

items.body: Register Login Three Under The Radar Pending Free Agents To Watch By Bradley Keith | at November 4, 2026 7:31 pm As the calendar turns to November, hovering around 20% of the 2026-27 NHL season completed, there’s still a lot to be unpacked before thinking of free agency next summer. This time last year few would have expected names like Ryan Shea to fetch a five-year deal in Edmonton, or for Daniel Vladař to become the guy in the crease for the Flyers, earning a long term extension . Of course you have future Hall of Famers like Erik Karlsson or Nikita Kucherov playing at their elite level to set up for a huge payday, wherever that may be. What about three lesser discussed names who so far are stepping up at the most opportune time, trending in the direction of becoming highly sought after free agents? During the first period of Washington’s eventual 6-5 loss, Chychrun went awkwardly into the boards behind the Capitals’ net while making a puck recovery on a power play. The feet-first collision knocked the skate blade out of his right skate and left him immobile right in front of goaltender Logan Thompson . The high-scoring defenseman immediately shouted for help from his teammates and he got it from captain Alex Ovechkin , who propelled Chychrun toward Washington’s bench with a couple of spears to the fallen defender’s rear end. No, that isn’t running back Saquon Barkley executing the Philadelphia Eagles’ famous Tush Push by shoving quarterback Jalen Hurts over the pile to earn a first down; it’s the greatest goal scorer in the history of the NHL jabbing his good pal in the rump to help save the remaining time on Washington’s power play. With Ovechkin’s assistance, the near-helpless Chychrun could quickly get off the ice for repairs, replaced by Cole Hutson with nearly 90 seconds remaining on the man advantage. Ovechkin has recorded plenty of assists during his career, still just two shy of overtaking Nicklas Backstrom for Washington’s all-time franchise lead, but he won’t see his name on the scoresheet for this one. Despite the quicker-than-usual end to his power-play shift and time on the bench to get a new blade installed, Chychrun still led all skaters in the game with 26:50 of ice time. items.title: Canadiens pick up the pieces after ’embarrassing, unacceptable’ collapse against Jets
items.body: The Montreal Canadiens were still digesting their epic, history-making collapse a little more than 12 hours later. In a stunning turnaround that made headlines across North America — Fox News called it a "choke job almost too shocking to believe" — the Canadiens surrendered a four-goal lead with 2:39 remaining in regulation and lost 5-4 in overtime to the Winnipeg Jets on Tuesday night. "I don't know, it's hard right now," veteran centre Jake Evans said after practice Wednesday morning. "I think we're all still swallowing it up." It was the latest four-goal comeback in NHL history, smashing the previous mark by more than four minutes. Teams had a record of 0-10,299-0 when facing a deficit of at least four goals entering the final three minutes of regulation before Tuesday. The Jets scored four goals in 126 seconds to erase the lead. You have to go back to Jan. 21, 1919, when Montreal gave up four goals in 100 seconds against the Toronto Arenas, to find a faster stretch of four goals against in Canadiens history. "It's hard to explain," said head coach Martin St. Louis, whose playing career spanned 1,134 NHL games. "I've never been part of something like that." St. Louis is known for his optimistic, inspirational approach to coaching. He was relatively calm in his post-game news conference Tuesday but made clear a day later he wasn’t glossing over the jaw-dropping defeat as the Canadiens (9-3-3) prepare to host the Utah Mammoth on Thursday. items.title: How teams and star players would benefit from shorter-term contracts

items.body: Dylan Larkin asked for a trade in year four of an eight-year deal. Connor Hellebuyck asked for a trade in year three of a seven-year deal. Brady Tkachuk made it to year six of his before he wanted out, which was granted before year seven began. All of these players wielded no-trade clauses that hampered any potential return their teams could get, which was a bad deal for the fans twice — they lost a star, and recouped little for him. For these and other elite NHLers, I understand the desire to sign for eight years the second you have a team willing to give it to you. But when it came to these truly top-end guys, the “give me the max dollars and length” always felt like contracts written with crayons rather than calligraphy. Sure you're able to get a big long-term deal, but if you're a proven top-end player in the NHL, wouldn't you want to maintain some flexibility on where you play? The way Auston Matthews has done his contracts has always made sense to me. He's signed five- and four-year contracts after his entry-level deal with the Leafs and has made good money, but never sought out maximum length. Five years is a big commitment to a city, isn’t it? items.title: Voters reject proposed taxes tied to planned new arena for Dallas Stars
items.summary: Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL’s Stars.
items.body: PLANO, Texas — Voters in a Dallas suburb have rejected a proposition that would have authorized new taxes related to a planned new arena for the NHL's Stars. Unofficial results from Tuesday's vote in the city of Plano showed 54.6 per cent of the more than 102,000 votes cast were against the single ballot proposal to authorize taxes on tickets, parking, car rentals, hotel rooms and the professional teams that would use the arena. Those taxes were to help the city pay off up to $700 million in bonds it has committed to the proposed $3 billion mixed-use development that would include the new arena. The vote was about the proposed taxes, and not whether the $1-billion arena could be built as part of a large-scale redevelopment project of The Shops at Willow Bend, where the last enclosed mall built in Texas is being demolished. It could include sports, entertainment, retail, dining and public gathering spaces. “The proposed redevelopment at The Shops at Willow Bend remains an important opportunity for our community," Plano Mayor John Muns said in a statement. “We are committed to thoughtful reinvestment and responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars as we consider what comes next.” The hockey-specific arena would be owned by the city, with the Stars intending to lease it for 30 years. Stars officials hope to move in 2031 about 20 miles north of the downtown American Airlines Center, which they have shared with the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks since it opened in 2001. The leases at the AAC for both teams expire in 2031, and the Mavericks have plans for a similar project of their own away from downtown, about 10 miles north on the former site of a Dallas mall.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images A veteran netminder is set to get his wheels under him once again. On Wednesday, the New York Rangers announced that goaltender Joonas Korpisalo has been assigned to their American Hockey League affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack, on a conditioning assignment. Per NHL rules, a conditioning stint can last no longer than 14 days. The reason Korpisalo is heading back to the minors is to get in shape after missing a considerable amount of time. The 32-year-old suffered a lower-body injury in the opening days of the 2026-27 season, leading to him being placed on injured reserve. It still isn’t clear when or where Korpisalo suffered the injury. He backed up Igor Shesterkin for the team’s season opener last month. He did appear in one preseason game for the Blueshirts, making 20 saves in a shootout win over the New Jersey Devils. Korpisalo came to Broadway over the summer, as the Boston Bruins traded the Finnish backstop to the Blueshirts for prospect Kalle Vaisanen and a fourth-round pick in the 2028 NHL Draft. Korpisalo had spent the past two seasons with the Bruins, mainly serving as a backup to Jeremy Swayman. In 2025-26, he posted a record of 14-9-6, with a 3.15 goals-against average, a .894 save percentage and one shutout. In 334 regular-season appearances in his NHL career, Korpisalo is 140-126-38, with a 3.06 GAA, a .900 SV% and eight shutouts. He’s in the fourth season of a five-year contract, which he signed with the Ottawa Senators in July 2023. items.body: VANCOUVER — Asked about the opportunity he is getting with the Vancouver Canucks , Jacob Quillan said: “This is everything.” A scoring star in college, the 24-year-old showed Tuesday night he is willing to do anything to stay in the National Hockey League by delivering the hit of the game and then fighting twice as the Canucks lost 5-4 to the Anaheim Ducks at Rogers Arena. Quillan did fine in his first two NHL fights when challenged by six-foot-five Roger McQueen, then rugged defenceman Travis Mitchell. He can’t build his career on fighting. But his willingness to stand up for himself — to show his new Canuck teammates he will fight for them — was notable on a night when Vancouver couldn’t survive its penalty killing or Ducks sniper Cutter Gauthier, but literally and figuratively battled their way back into the game against one of the league’s biggest teams. It was another game in which the rebuilding Canucks, even with their many flaws, were fully engaged, combative and played their opponents even at five-on-five. Down three goals in the third period, the Canucks surged back with a pair of goals from Jake DeBrusk and generated significant offensive-zone pressure at the end. items.title: Canadiens on wrong side of history in skid-stopping comeback win for Jets
items.summary: No matter how poorly the Canadiens played, they were in the best position possible with the clock ticking down, and then they inexcusably crumbled.
items.body: MONTREAL — This was a bad game from start to finish for the Montreal Canadiens , but to suggest it ended the way it should’ve — with the Winnipeg Jets making NHL history to avoid a 10th straight loss — would be bending the truth. For the Canadiens had a 4-0 lead with 2:40 to play, and when Cole Caufield , who scored two of their goals, said it should’ve ended well before they lost in overtime, he was right. No matter how poorly his team played, it was in the best position it could possibly be in with the clock ticking down, and then it inexcusably crumbled. Four Jets goals in 2:39, and one more from Dylan Samberg with 1:30 to go in overtime, sealed the Canadiens’ fate. Afterwards, Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis said, “We got smacked in the teeth and maybe that’s what we needed as a team,” and he was also probably right. This year's class includes Carey Price , Pekka Rinne , Patrice Bergeron , Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the Player category and Brian Burke in the Builder category. Here, NHL.com senior writer Tracey Myers profiles Burke. Brian Burke was 12 years old when his life trajectory unknowingly was set during a family move from Boston to Minnesota. “The moving trucks got stuck in a blizzard in Pennsylvania with all our furniture and stuff, so we were stuck in a hotel for three nights in Bloomington, Minnesota,” Burke said. “The state high-school hockey tournament was on. That’s when I fell in love with the game, watching high-school hockey.” That love affair has lasted Burke’s entire life, and the 71-year-old has been one of the most impactful people in so many areas of hockey. "When I think of his image, the thing that first pops into my head, he used to have a picture in his office at the League of him on the ice in a Maine Mariners uniform with blood all over his face," NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said. "That's one image that he gives off, but the other image is somebody who's concerned about people, embraces people and relationships, and if you're his friend, he'll go to all ends of the Earth to support you and be there for you, which is the mark of a truly good human being." Burke's NHL career began in 1987 when he was named vice president and director of hockey operations for the Vancouver Canucks. Then In 1992, he became general manager of the Hartford Whalers. items.body: NHL Commissioner writes special testimonial for friend, colleague A few months after Gary Bettman was named the first Commissioner in NHL History on Feb. 1, 1993, he hired Brian Burke to be the League’s senior vice president and director of hockey operations. Burke served as the League’s chief disciplinarian, and he oversaw the on-ice officials. He also worked with Bettman on League direction and collective bargaining matters. Burke left his League job in 1998 to become president and general manager of the Vancouver Canucks, but he remains a great friend of Bettman, who Burke considers one of his mentors. There are few people who have had such a diverse career in the game and there are few people who have been as committed to the game both on and off the ice as Brian Burke. In addition to all the work he’s done either as a player or an agent or an executive at the club level or League level, he’s always been a part of giving back, using the game as a platform to be involved in the community. This week spotlights a unique New York Rangers broadcaster whose other life happens to be as chief operating officer of a thriving Brooklyn beverage company. There are not enough hours in a 24-hour day for Dave Starman, but somehow he makes do with his dream job and family business. Between his role as radio analyst of the New York Rangers and chief operating officer of the Autotap Corporation, Starman, 58, is busier than a paperhanger with an itch. "I adore every minute of it," Starman said in an email, "and I never get tired because I love both my jobs." Autotap is service provider of fountain beverage services started by Starman's great grandfather, Joseph, in 1900 and incorporated in 1925. "My job is to supervise sales, service and installation of fountain beverage equipment, soda, beer and wine systems," Starman said. "I also keep track of 10 trucks handling delivery routes throughout the city." And without taking a deep breath, Starman personally answers every customer email "because we care about them." Yeah, it keeps him busy, but not too busy for hockey, his lifetime love. A passionate affection for the Rangers, and being a goalie, has been part of Starman's life since he was knee-high to a grasshopper, growing up in Belle Harbor, New York, on the Rockaway Peninsula in Queens. "I played goal for the Greater New York Stars and later the University of Hartford," he said, "and drifted into coaching with a youth hockey team in Connecticut. items.title: Jets pull record latest four-goal comeback in NHL history to end drought
items.summary: The Jets had lost nine straight games prior to the shocking late-game effort.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources If any Winnipeg Jets fans left the Bell Centre early to beat the traffic, you’re in for a rude awakening. The Jets failed to score through 57:21 against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday. But after Tyrel Bauer scored his first career goal, everything changed. The Jets ended up scoring three more goals to complete the latest four-goal comeback victory in NHL history. The previous record was set on Nov. 10, 2007, when the Los Angeles Kings scored four goals against Dallas after the 52:46 mark. According to the NHL, this is just the fourth time this has occured after the 50:00 mark, and just the first to have it happen in the final five minutes of a game. Montreal looked in full control, with Owen Beck, Josh Anderson, Cole Caufield (twice) finding the back of the net. Bauer’s goal put an end to Jacob Fowler’s shutout effort, and, seemingly, that felt like the only thing the Jets could get excited about. Instead, Morgan Barron scored less than a minute later, and Kyle Connor made it a one-goal game at 19:00. Just 27 seconds later, Connor recorded his second of the night and 13th of the season, sending the game in overtime after the Jets scored four goals in 2:39 of regulation. Winnipeg wouldn’t stop there. At 3:30 in overtime, Dylan Samberg’s snap shot would beat Fowler to give the Jets the stunning overtime victory, ending the team’s nine-game losing streak in the process. Their last win came on October 13, a 5-2 victory over Minnesota. The Jets finished the game with a 47-22 shot advantage. Notably, this was Montreal’s first game with the club’s new Hometown Remix jersey. The Jets will look to keep the momentum alive on Nov. 5 when the team hosts the Vancouver Canucks.

items.summary:

items.body: Kevin Lowe was happy to see his record broken by Ryan Nugent-Hopkins . The Hockey Hall of Famer congratulated the Edmonton Oilers forward on playing his 1,038 th game with the team, passing Lowe on the franchise’s games played list, in a video posted by Sportsnet on Tuesday. Kevin Lowe with a message to Ryan Nugent-Hopkins 🧡💙 pic.twitter.com/Ns6f2HKICI “Ryan, Congratulations on becoming the all-time leader in regular seasons game played as an Edmonton Oiler,” Lowe said in the video message. “That record has stood around for 28 years and I’ve been extremely proud of it. “But as we all know, records are meant to be broken. So, if someone is going to take it away from me, I couldn’t think of a more popular Oiler to do it.” The six-time Stanley Cup winner played 15 of his 19 NHL seasons with the Oilers, amounting to 1,037 games. Before the Oilers game against the New Jersey Devils, the team celebrated Nugent-Hopkins’ record with custom T-shirts as they arrived at Prudential Center. In the second period, Nugent-Hopkins netted a power play goal to mark his milestone game. He also recorded an assist on defenseman Evan Bouchard ’s first period goal. Nugent-Hopkins is in his 16 th season with the Oilers, who drafted him with the No. 1 pick in the 2011 NHL Draft. He has 295 goals and 518 assists in his 1,038 games with the team.

items.title: Oilers fall to Hellebuyck, Devils in shootout
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Jack Hughes scored two goals and had an assist, Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves to win his first home start of the season, and the New Jersey Devils halted the Edmonton Oilers ' winning streak at three with a 4-3 shootout decision on Tuesday night. Fans chanted “USA! USA!” after Hughes' first goal, a nod to him scoring the winner in overtime to deliver gold for the U.S. at the Olympics against Canada in the final. Hellebuyck, who backstopped the Americans in Milan, was making his third start for the Devils since they traded for him. Arseny Gritsyuk got the shootout winner and Connor Brown also scored in regulation against the Oilers, who he played with for two seasons and helped reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2024 and '25. The Devils have won two in a row and five of their past six. Connor McDavid extended his NHL record season-opening assist streak to 16 games with his league-leading 31st. Evan Bouchard, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Leon Draisaitl scored for Edmonton, and Tristan Jarry had his shutout streak ended after more than seven periods without allowing a goal but finished with 31 saves. Skating in his 1,038th regular season game, Nugent-Hopkins broke a tie with Hall of Famer Kevin Lowe for the most in Oilers franchise history. Players wore T-shirts with that number and a caricature of Nugent-Hopkins on it. Edmonton was without fellow forward Isaac Howard, who coach Mike Babcock said will miss a couple of weeks with a left knee injury that is not considered a long-term issue. Forward Trent Frederic was a healthy scratch, while defenceman Jake Walman returned after missing the past three. Oilers: Open a four-game homestand Thursday against the Anaheim Ducks.

items.body: Register Login Miro Heiskanen Exits Game With Upper-Body Injury By Ryan Long | at November 3, 2026 9:17 pm Stars defenseman Miro Heiskanen left and did not return to tonight’s game against the Capitals due to an upper-body injury, the team announced. Heiskanen exited after his first shift of the second period, during which he took a hit from Capitals forward Justin Sourdif . While the severity of the injury remains to be seen, any absence would be a significant loss for Dallas’ blue line. The 27-year-old entered tonight with three goals and 11 points in 14 games while averaging 25:58 of ice time. He continues to anchor the Stars’ top pairing alongside fellow Finn Esa Lindell . The two logged roughly 1,022 minutes together last season, the seventh-most of any defense pair in the league. Heiskanen is also central to both of Dallas’ special teams units. Last season, he was the only player in the NHL to average more than three minutes per game on both the power play (3:27) and the penalty kill (3:06). Those minutes came in a strong bounce-back year. After a knee injury and surgery cost him most of the 2024-25 campaign, Heiskanen posted 63 points (nine goals, 54 assists) in 77 games last season. He ranked ninth among NHL defensemen in scoring and fourth among all players in average ice time at 25:28, and he set a career high with 132 blocked shots. He also helped Finland win bronze at the 2026 Winter Olympics with five points in six games and led all Olympic skaters in average ice time. The third overall pick in 2017 entered tonight with 357 career points in 566 games and is 13 assists shy of 300. items.summary: Brayden Point scored two goals, Anthony Cirelli got one and the Tampa Bay Lightning beat the Detroit Red Wings 4-2 on Tuesday night for their seventh straight home win.
items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Brayden Point scored two goals, Anthony Cirelli got one and the Tampa Bay Lightning beat the Detroit Red Wings 4-2 on Tuesday night for their seventh straight home win. Reigning NHL MVP Nikita Kucherov had two assists in his first home game since asking the Lightning for a trade, and goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 19 shots. Lucas Raymond and J.T. Compher scored Detroit’s goals. The Red Wings pulled their goalie for an extra shooter for the final three minutes and put plenty of pressure on Vasilevskiy but couldn't get the tying goal. Ryan McDonagh slid an empty-netter down the ice with 1 second left. Point gave the Lightning 1-0 lead with a power-play goal in the first period. He didn’t quite get everything on his shot in the low slot off Kucherov’s centering pass but it went past goalie John Gibson. Point snapped a shot over Gibson’s glove 5:07 later to make it 2-0. Kucherov set it up with another perfect pass. Gibson was replaced by Daniil Tarasov to start the second period after stopping 11 of 13 shots in the first. Cirelli lifted his fifth goal past Tarasov into the top left corner for a 3-0 lead in the second period. Raymond fired a shot from the left point past Vasilevskiy midway through the second to cut it to 3-1. The Red Wings got within 3-2 less than six minutes into the third when Compher scored a power-play goal, blasting a shot from the right circle underneath Vasilevskiy’s left pad. items.body: Register Login John Gibson Exits Game With Lower-Body Injury By Ryan Long | at November 3, 2026 8:04 pm Red Wings goaltender John Gibson left tonight’s game against the Lightning with a lower-body injury and will not return, the team announced . Gibson allowed two goals on 11 shots while playing the entire first period, and it isn’t exactly clear when he was hurt. If he misses more time, Daniil Tarasov would take over as Detroit’s starter and the Red Wings would need to recall a goaltender from AHL Grand Rapids to fill out the roster. This is the second time in less than two weeks that Gibson has left a game early. He sat out the third period of Detroit’s 5-2 win over the Canucks on October 22 with what the team called an upper-body injury, but he was back in net two days later in Calgary. The 33-year-old has struggled early this season. Gibson came into tonight 4-5-1 with a 3.37 GAA and an .860 save percentage in 10 appearances. That’s a sharp drop from his first season in Detroit, when he went 29-22-4 with a 2.72 GAA and a .901 save percentage in 57 games, his heaviest workload since 2018-19. He is in the final year of his contract, which carries a $6.4MM cap hit. Tarasov has been strong in limited work since signing a one-year, $2MM deal with Detroit in free agency on July 1. In his first start with the club, the 27-year-old stopped all 30 shots he faced in regulation and overtime in a 1-0 shootout loss in Montreal. In Grand Rapids, Michal Postava has opened the AHL season 5-0 with a 1.20 GAA and a .955 save percentage. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images As if Hockeytown needs even more bad news. As the second period between the Detroit Red Wings and Tampa Bay Lightning began Tuesday night, Red Wings goaltender John Gibson didn’t take the ice. The team later announced that Gibson wouldn’t return to the contest due to a lower-body injury. Gibson gave up two goals on 13 shots in the opening 20 minutes, as the Red Wings found themselves trailing 2-0 heading into the first intermission. Daniil Tarasov entered the game in relief, less than 24 hours after earning the win against his former team, the Florida Panthers . This is far from the first time Gibson has been hurt in his NHL career, and it isn’t the first time he’s had to prematurely leave a game this season. Back on Oct. 22, he suffered an upper-body injury in a game against the Vancouver Canucks , but returned to the crease two nights later. While it’s too early to tell the severity of Gibson’s injury and how long he could be out of action, Detroit doesn’t have a whole lot of time to waste, as the team returns home on Thursday night to host the Vegas Golden Knights. If Gibson’s injury is more than a small tweak, expect Michal Postava to be called up from the Grand Rapids Griffins, the Red Wings’ American Hockey League affiliate. Postava picked up a win in his first NHL start last Monday and was just named the AHL’s goaltender of the month. Gibson has been Detroit’s No. 1 netminder since he came to the Original Six franchise in June 2025. However, he hasn’t nearly had as strong a start to this season as he did last year. In his first 10 starts, the 33-year-old is 4-5-1, with a 3.37 goals-against average and an .860 save percentage.

The baby-faced forward has been through the ups-and-downs of the franchise and is being rewarded for his efforts. Just about anyone who has played for the Edmonton Oilers knows how tough the market can be. You're forever in the spotlight, forever judged against some of the greatest talent in hockey history, forever judged by how many Stanley Cup championships you've won. Having the staying power of being a lifelong Oiler is something very few NHLers can say they have. This is what you have to keep in mind when you consider the career of Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. The 33-year-old has played 1,037 regular-season games with Edmonton – and on Tuesday night, he'll set the franchise record for games-played, surpassing Oilers icon Kevin Lowe for that honor. items.title: Prime Minister Mark Carney says Russia will not be allowed to compete at world juniors
items.body: Prime Minister Mark Carney says Russia will not be allowed to compete at next month's World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta. Carney, speaking in Antigua at the Commonwealth Summit, said Russian and Belarusian athletes will not be permitted to represent their countries in Canada as long as the war in Ukraine continues. His comments come after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled Friday that Russia must be reinstated to international hockey competition, starting with the world junior tournament. Several European hockey federations, including Sweden, Finland, Czechia and Latvia, have said their teams will refuse to face Russia. Hockey Canada says it has been consulting with the International Ice Hockey Federation and other stakeholders about the potential impact on the tournament.

Today, the Sharks announced they recalled defenseman Eric Pohlkamp from the AHL’s San Jose Barracuda. San Jose selected Pohlkamp, 22, with the 132nd overall (fifth-round) pick in the 2023 NHL Draft. The Sharks drafted forward Will Smith with the fourth overall pick in the same draft. As a rebuilding club, it’s imperative that the Sharks hit on their higher-tier draft selections, which they have done so far. However, potential diamond-in-the-rough players like Pohlkamp could send this organization into one of its most successful stretches in franchise history. During his draft season, Pohlkamp was playing his second season with the USHL’s Cedar Rapids RoughRiders. Like many smaller defensemen, he flashed his offensive upside, scoring 16 goals and 51 points in 59 games with a -1 rating. The Brainerd, MN, native committed to Bemidji State University for the 2023-24 campaign. He played well, finishing with 11 goals and 24 points in 32 games with a +4 rating, leading the Beavers to the CCHA Conference Championship against Michigan Tech. Pohlkamp made the All-CCHA Rookie Team and All-CCHA First Team at season’s end. His impressive freshman campaign drew national attention, culminating in his transfer to the University of Denver. It couldn’t have been a better position. Throughout his two years with the Pioneers, Pohlkamp dominated, scoring 29 goals and 74 points in 87 games with a staggering +55 rating. items.title: Taking stock of early NHL playoff picture
items.summary: Nearing the official quarter mark of the season, Rory Boylen took a look at some positive and negative indicators for the teams in the playoff picture.
items.body: Things have changed on the NHL calendar this season. There are two more games, for one. And with that, the season started a little earlier than usual. Normally we would use the Nov. 1 benchmark to compare seasons to one another, but this year we'll do it a little differently. We are now 35 days into the NHL season — about two weeks shy of the official quarter mark — and that's the number we'll use when looking back at where we were a season ago. It's obviously far too early to draw any grand conclusions about the playoffs. It is too early to play your way in, but you can start to play your way out of the post-season if early indicators don't start to improve. But we should keep things in perspective. items.body: Center has four points in 14 games this season; Seattle receives Wood in return Shane Wright was traded to the Nashville Predators by the Seattle Kraken for Matthew Wood on Sunday. Wright, the No. 4 pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, has four points (three goals, one assist) in 14 games this season. The center played 167 games with the Kraken since the start of 2024-25 after playing the majority of the previous season with Coachella Valley of the American Hockey League. "I was surprised, but I was excited as well," Wright said Monday. "Really unbelievable city and organization. I'm excited to be here. "I think, for me, I always wanted a little more opportunity. I wanted to have more minutes. I wanted to play a bigger role, whether that was in Seattle or somewhere else. I was happy to do that, but I'm moving on from the situation and happy to be here. I'm still young, so I want to hopefully be here for a number of years, build something special here and be part of a winning culture and a winning group." The 22-year-old has 82 points (39 goals, 43 assists) in 183 NHL games. Wright had nine points (two goals, seven assists) in 24 AHL playoff games in 2023, helping Coachella Valley reach the Calder Cup Finals before losing to Hershey. "For us, we just felt it made sense for quite a few reasons," Predators general manager Chris MacFarland said. "We're excited to add Shane. We feel he's a natural fit in the middle of the ice. We feel we've got a great opportunity for him to improve day by day. He'll be a better player in the spring than he is now, and he'll be a better player next fall than he is now. We hope the same for Matthew. This is one that you hope works out for both teams." The Predators (5-4-5) host the Carolina Hurricanes on Tuesday (8 p.m. ET; HHN, CARNHL, SCRIPPS, SN+).

items.title: Calgary Flames Legend Jaroma Iginla Battling Neurological Issues
items.summary: The 49-year-old revealed he is dealing with undiagnosed issues that have impacted his energy, weight and speech.
items.body: Brett Holmes-USA TODAY Sports Brett Holmes-USA TODAY Sports Calgary Flames Legend Jaroma Iginla Battling Neurological Issues Eric Cruikshank Partner Nov 3, 2026 9:29 PM Published Nov 3, 2026 9:29 PM The 49-year-old revealed he is dealing with undiagnosed issues that have impacted his energy, weight and speech. One of the NHL's most iconic stars is facing a difficult battle off the ice. Calgary Flames icon Jarome Iginla is dealing with health issues that have impacted his, the Hall of Famer revealed in an interview with Sportsnet's Eric Francis on Tuesday. "Some neurological issues," Iginla told Francis. "I'm not entirely sure what it is, it may be from metal toxins from reaction to cobalt hip. "I need more time to figure it all out, but I’m still hopeful that I will recover fully." After a 20-year career in the NHL, Iginla underwent hip replacement surgery a few years ago. Complications as a result of the surgery as well as some medications arose, which have impacted his energy, weight and speech. Francis added that Iginla has been tested and has met with numerous medical professionals for over a year to get a clearer idea of what the 49-year-old is dealing with. Concerns for Iginla's health circulated around social media by fans over the past week after a short clip from Amazon Prime's "Hometown Giants" series revealed Iginla's condition had noticeably changed. The show follows the WHL's Vancouver Giants, the team which Iginla's son, Joe, plays for. Jarome's son Tij was selected sixth overall by the Utah Mammoth in 2024, while the Flames drafted Joe in June. His daughter, Jade, was drafted this summer by PWHL Hamilton.
